title: Common
description: Shared definitions for harness contracts. Not an instance schema.

Id.description: Opaque identifier (org, session, run, attempt, invocation, record ...).

PrincipalRef.description: Reference to a principal set by Node at admission; resolved by PrincipalResolver.

SessionRole.description: A participant's role in the session a run belongs to: its owner, or a collaborator the owner shared it with (ARCHITECTURE 4.9).

ModelToolName.description: Tool name as shown to the model; unique per run.

Name.description: Lower-case machine name (provider, transport, resolver, rule ...).

Digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON (or raw bytes for blobs).

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp with a literal Z. Kept a string so digests never depend on a parser's re-formatting.

UInt.description: Non-negative integer within the IEEE-754 safe range, so it survives JavaScript.

Usd.description: US dollars, at most a billion (well inside JavaScript's safe integers).

ref.description: Where the content is: `sealed:` (Node's sealed store) or `inline:` (the bytes themselves, base64url). One bound for every receiver, events and a child's result alike (CHILDREF): the longest inline ref anyone writes is Node's steering message (100,000 characters of UTF-8, 400,007 characters inlined); the worker's store seals what would not fit.

ContentRef.description: Claim-checked content in CAS; hash and size are verified on read.

inputIncludesCached.description: true: inputTokens counts cacheReadTokens and cacheWriteTokens. Absent on a usage with no cached tokens and on events written before USAGE1, whose inputTokens is the reporter's own count.

RiskClass.description: A tool's risk class (OWD-7), ranked read < write_internal < write_external < destructive < financial: its effect and sink, unless its metadata marks it as one that cannot be undone (a delete, a send) or that moves money. Metadata for policy and audit; which calls ask stays the approval rules' decision.

Effect.description: A tool's effect class: what it does to the world, ranked read < workspace < write < execute.

RunKind.description: command: a person's /run (SLASH3), one run_code call and no model; its turn is never in a later turn's context.

Via.description: How the actor reached the run: a browser session, a personal access token, an OAuth app, a trigger, or a service (the Slack bot, a service account). Node derives it from the credential, never from a request body.

AccessAccountKind.description: Whose account a model call uses and how it is held (ARCHITECTURE §4.6.1 AccountKind).

AccessRouteKind.description: How a model call reaches the vendor (ARCHITECTURE §4.6.1 RouteKind).

Writer.description: Who appends a journal event: Node (admission, decisions, run transitions) or the worker.

Visibility.description: Who may read a journal event: the run's owner, every participant, or audit only.

RunStatus.description: A run's lifecycle state; completed, failed, cancelled and quarantined are terminal.

SuspendReason.description: Why a run is suspended (run.suspended). retired: an operator retired the run's engine version (ADR-OPS-01 D6); Node suspends it and resumes it when the version is allowed again or the release declares a successor.

YieldReason.description: Why a run yielded its slot until notBefore (run.yielded); payload_store_unavailable is written by Node only; sandbox_wait: the sandbox broker could not make or reach a sandbox; store_wait: a store an engine run saves to (its blob objects, or the workspace store) could not be reached; preempted: a lower priority class gave its slot to a higher one at a step boundary (G-45), written only to a Node that names priority_preemption.

PriorityClass.description: Which runs go first when work waits for a slot (G-45), highest first: interactive (a person waits on it), approval_resume (a lower-class run a person just answered), background (a schedule or workflow), batch (bulk work nobody waits on). Applied to the run claim queue, the model gateway's concurrency and the shared vendor rate budget; every lower class is owed a floor share, so none starves.

CutShortReason.description: Which limit cut a completed run's work short (run.completed.truncatedBy): its spending limit (budget), its turn limit (turns), its working time (time), its steps repeating without progress (stall, BU-06), a model provider that stayed unavailable past the run's bounded wait (provider, WP-77), a coding engine that ended its turn on an error of its own, not a PipesHub refusal (engine_error, WP-84), or a model request PipesHub blocked because it looked like it carried a secret (secret_blocked, WP-103). The run still answered, from what it had gathered, on one answer-only final turn.

VendorRuleStatus.description: A vendor rule's standing under the vendor's terms (A1).

ToolErrorCode.description: Why a tool call failed, as the person reads it (ERR-UX): the code beside the redacted detail the model reads (the tool outcome's result document `errorCode`). unavailable: the tool's service could not be reached or is down; timeout: it did not answer in time; rate_limited: it is limiting requests; auth: it refused the connection's credentials; not_found: what the call named does not exist; invalid_call: the model called the tool wrongly; failed: anything else.

RequestedEffort.description: The reasoning effort a run's model policy asks for (run-spec `modelPolicy.reasoningEffort`, kept inline there); every engine profile effort (ProfileEffort) is one, and `minimal` narrows a profile to `low`.

Offering.description: Which offering an install is (A1, AGENT_HARNESS_OFFERING); vendor rules allow some routes only in some offerings. An edition may add its own offerings (x-extensible-enum).
